```{r}

library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)
data("ny_noaa")

ny_noaa

ny_noaa_df = ny_noaa |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10, 
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = as.numeric(month),
    day = as.numeric(day))
  
#used AI for finding out how to separate; specifically sep = "-"
  
ny_noaa_df

```

The original dataset is a tibble that is 7 columns and 2,595,176 rows. The data is divided by ID number which appears to be the same for each row. Other key variables are `date`, `pcrp`, 
`snow`, `snwd`, `tmax`, and `tmin`. 


```{r}

ny_noaa_df |> 
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") |>
  arrange(desc(n_obs)) |>
  filter(min_rank(desc(n_obs)) < 11) |>
  knitr::kable()
  
#Used arrange to order from most common to least
#Filter helps make the list smaller

```

Some of the most commonly observed values for snowfall include 0 mm, NA, 25 mm, 13 mm,and 51 mm. 0mm being first makes sense since it doesn't snow in New York at lot over the course of the year.

#Looking at average max temperature now

```{r}

ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1,7)) |>
  mutate(month = case_when(
    month == 1 ~ "January",
    month == 7 ~ "July")) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y=mean_tmax, color = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
#Used AI assistance to mutate using case_when to switch numbers to month terms. Also used AI assistance to get rid of the legend by using theme(legend.position = "none")

  
```

The mean temperature in January is much lower compared to the mean temperature in July. This result is expected. The temperature fluctuates more in January in a zig zap (up and down) appearance over the years. The temperature in July appears to have less variation. There are some outliers in the graphs. For instance, one outlier shows a very cold July year around 1988.


```{r}

install.packages("hexbin")

tmax_tmin_df =
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex()

tmax_tmin_df

#using geom_hex() here since lots of data

snow_dist =
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100)
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex()
  


```
